edits.text: 1. PURPOSE; CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION. The parties wish to explore a potential transaction (the “Purpose”) and may disclose confidential or proprietary information to one another in connection with the Purpose. “Confidential Information” means information disclosed by or on behalf of a party (the “Disclosing Party”) to the other party (the “Receiving Party”), in any form, that is marked or identified as confidential or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given its nature or the circumstances of disclosure. Confidential Information includes the existence and status of discussions between the parties and the terms of this Agreement. The Receiving Party shall use Confidential Information solely to evaluate, negotiate, or, if agreed, consummate the Purpose, and shall not disclose it except as expressly permitted by this Agreement.
edits.name: 1. PURPOSE; CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION

edits.text: 2. PROTECTION; PERMITTED DISCLOSURES. The Receiving Party shall protect Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own similar information, and no less than reasonable care. It may disclose Confidential Information only to its and its affiliates’ directors, officers, employees, financing sources, and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose and are bound by confidentiality obligations or professional duties at least as protective as this Agreement. The Receiving Party is responsible for any breach of this Agreement by its representatives. These obligations do not apply to information the Receiving Party can demonstrate: (a) is or becomes publicly available through no breach of this Agreement; (b) was lawfully known to it without restriction before disclosure; (c) is received lawfully from a third party without a duty of confidentiality; or (d) is independently developed without use of or reference to Confidential Information. If disclosure is required by law or legal process, the Receiving Party may disclose only the portion legally required and, to the extent legally permitted, shall give the Disclosing Party prompt notice and reasonably cooperate, at the Disclosing Party’s expense, in seeking protective treatment. The Receiving Party shall protect Confidential Information for five years from its disclosure; however, information qualifying as a trade secret shall be protected for so long as it remains a trade secret under applicable law.
edits.name: 2. PROTECTION; PERMITTED DISCLOSURES

edits.text: 3. TERM. This Agreement remains in effect for twenty-four months from the date of signing, unless the parties agree in writing to extend it. Expiration or termination shall not affect obligations that by their terms survive, including the confidentiality and use restrictions in Section 2.
edits.name: 3. TERM

edits.text: 4. RETURN OR DESTRUCTION; REMEDIES. Upon the Disclosing Party’s written request, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy its Confidential Information, except that it may retain copies required by law or held in routine electronic backups, in each case subject to this Agreement for so long as retained. A party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief for any actual or threatened breach, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity. Neither party shall be liable under this Agreement for indirect, incidental, special, punitive, or consequential damages.
edits.name: 4. RETURN OR DESTRUCTION; REMEDIES

drafter.private_reasoning: Preserve the client's protection against consequential-damages exposure while offering a targeted carve-out for breaches of confidentiality or use restrictions and specified serious misconduct. Accept the requested narrowing for affiliates and financing sources; retain and clarify Receiving Party responsibility for representatives. Do not disclose confidential client information.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you. We have narrowed permitted disclosure to affiliates and financing sources directly involved in the Purpose, and clarified that the Receiving Party remains responsible for its representatives’ breaches. On damages, rather than deleting the exclusion in full, we propose retaining a mutual exclusion for indirect and specified damages, with a carve-out for breaches of the confidentiality or use obligations and for fraud or willful misconduct. We believe this preserves a proportionate allocation of risk while ensuring meaningful recourse for misuse or disclosure of Confidential Information.

It may disclose Confidential Information only to its and its affiliates’ directors, officers, employees, financing sources, and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose; provided that any affiliate or financing source receiving Confidential Information must be directly involved in evaluating, negotiating, financing, or consummating the Purpose. If disclosure is required by law or legal process, the Receiving Party may disclose only the portion legally required and, to the extent legally permitted, shall give the Disclosing Party prompt notice and reasonably cooperate, at the Disclosing Party’s expense, in seeking protective treatment. The Receiving Party shall protect Confidential Information for five years from its disclosure; however, information qualifying as a trade secret shall be protected for so long as it remains a trade secret under applicable law.

edits.text: 4. RETURN OR DESTRUCTION; REMEDIES. Upon the Disclosing Party’s written request, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy its Confidential Information, except that it may retain copies required by law or held in routine electronic backups, in each case subject to this Agreement for so long as retained. A party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief for any actual or threatened breach, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity. Neither party shall be liable under this Agreement for indirect, incidental, special, punitive, or consequential damages, except to the extent arising from a party’s breach of its confidentiality or use obligations under this Agreement, or its fraud or willful misconduct.
